title: Compute character-level CLM loss
description: This program compares uniform and frequency-based next-character probabilities with cross-entropy loss.

steps.description: The corpus supplies the training text. The code creates a sorted character vocabulary and prints its size.
Each corpus character becomes an integer token ID. The decoded prefix checks that the IDs map back to the original characters.
Counter counts token frequencies. better_probs assigns each token its corpus frequency, while uniform_prob gives every token the same probability.
clm_loss visits each next token, takes negative log probability, averages the losses, and exponentiates that average for perplexity.

steps.question: Which model has lower loss on this corpus?
steps.answer: The frequency model has lower loss because it gives higher probability to more frequent tokens.

steps.description: The uniform-model call uses one probability for every character.
The frequency-model call uses each true character's corpus frequency. The output reports lower loss and lower perplexity than the uniform model.
The final loop shows the first ten positions with a five-character context, the true next character, its frequency probability, and its individual loss.
